purpose: What we can say about the identity of the three Forever beta builds, and how each claim is supported. No claim here is 'verified' in the M1 sense (Blizzard-confirmed by this pipeline).

ribbit_archive.what_it_is: Third-party archive of raw responses from Blizzard's version service. I read the file contents myself; that Blizzard's service produced them is [2nd].

foreverdiff.what_it_is: Site claiming to read data from Blizzard's CDN. Displays 16-hex-character prefixes of BuildConfig/CDNConfig. [2nd]

builds.evidence: [2nd] two third-party sources agree; not confirmed against Blizzard by this pipeline

observations: CDNConfig changed twice for each build while BuildConfig stayed fixed, so BuildConfig (not CDNConfig) is the stable build identity.

Earlier wow_classic_beta snapshots (seqn 4012168: 5.5.0.62071; seqn 4017103/4017986: '1.0', BuildId 1) show the product name was used for other things before Forever. Do not assume the product name alone identifies a Forever build.
Executable name for the beta is reported as WowB.exe by a third-party bug report (2nd).

table_content_across_builds.foreverdiff_claim: All three builds have 83 tables and 63,825 entities; 69893 vs 69876 and 69913 vs 69893 are identical at entity level. [2nd]
table_content_across_builds.att_mirror_observation: M1 [V]: 33 CSV files (23 tables) labelled 69893 and 69913 are byte-identical in the ATT repository history.
table_content_across_builds.interpretation: The two observations are consistent with genuinely unchanged table data. This weakens (but does not disprove) the M1 hypothesis that ATT merely relabelled files. ATT's updater script re-downloads when the BUILD label changes, so identical bytes after a re-download would also be consistent with unchanged data. [?]

not_available_to_me: Blizzard's version service and CDN (not reachable from this environment)
